title: How big is the open model economy today?
summary:
My longest running agent testbed has been building the Interconnects Dashboard — an aggregator of all of the best data on open model adoption and performance from across the web. This dashboard is freely available and becoming quite useful. Still, all the measurements we have on open model adoption are incredibly imprecise. We have noisy platform metrics, marketing-related metrics from startups, and imperfect public evaluations. It takes an informed eye to figure out where things are going. These research notes are my current best approximations of where we stand.
 As with most things on Interconnects, our goal is to build well more value than we capture, so the data on the dashboard will remain free for the foreseeable future. These notes will be more raw than many of my articles, a place for sharing what I’m mulling over but don’t have complete evidence for (yet). They will be primarily paid, enabling me to speak more freely. If you work in AI policy or policy-facing research, please reach out to us and we can likely get discounted or free access.
 The primary question I wanted to address today is: What is the market for open model inference? Is it growing? Is it a rounding error relative to OpenAI/Anthropic?

title: datasette-apps 0.3a0
summary:
Release: datasette-apps 0.3a0 

 Datasette Apps adds support for hosting and editing custom HTML applications inside of Datasette.

 These can be created by hand, but it's easier to create them using LLMs via Datasette Agent . This release improves that integration:

 Apps can now be tagged in Datasette Agent chat messages by typing # , which autocompletes from the apps the user has permission to view.

 New app_add_stored_queries() and app_remove_stored_queries() tools let the agent manage which stored queries an app is allowed to call. Granting a write query requires approval from the user first.

 app_create() now checks that each requested stored query exists and that the user can view it, and asks the user to approve any write queries before the app is created.

 The "View app" buttons shown by the agent tools, and the links on # app references, now open the app full screen in the Datasette Agent panel.

 Tags: datasette , datasette-agent , datasette-apps

title: datasette-agent 0.5a0
summary:
Release: datasette-agent 0.5a0 

 This is a significant release of Datasette Agent . The most notable new feature is called the panel - it lets the agent chat open and then sit next to pages from Datasette, for example a table or query page.

 When combined with datasette-apps this means you can prompt a database-backed app into existence and then modify it from the chat that sits next to that app.

 You can try it by signing in with your GitHub account to agent.datasette.io .
